title: PRACTICE
use_cases: Use when practicing the application of subtext in character dialogue
Implement when experimenting with how different genres change the meaning of identical lines
Configure when designing short writing prompts for workshop participation
Use when teaching students how to move beyond literal interpretations of text
content:
Take fifteen minutes to choose one of the lines below (or make up one of your own) and work it into two different short dialogue exchanges, each with different subtext.

“Can you spare some change?”

“I’ll go for a swim, thanks.”

“It wasn’t like that before.”

If you get stuck, here's a tip I give students: Imagine the line in different genres. Any line spoken in the context of a horror story will likely have a much different meaning than when spoken in a romance.

When you're done, share your practice in The Write Practice Pro workshops and encourage each other.
